questions.q: Define the principal focus of a convex mirror and state its position relative to the mirror. What is the SI unit of focal length?
questions.a: The principal focus of a convex mirror is the point on the principal axis from which incident rays parallel to the axis appear to diverge after reflection; it lies behind the mirror (virtual focus). The SI unit of focal length is metre (m). A wrong answer that places the focus in front of the mirror reveals confusion with concave mirrors; omitting the unit shows lack of attention to measurement standards.

questions.q: A student says, "The focal length of a convex mirror is negative because the focus is behind the mirror." Using the Cartesian sign convention, explain why this statement is incorrect.
questions.a: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light are positive. For a convex mirror, the incident light travels from the object towards the mirror; the focus is behind the mirror, i.e., opposite to the incident light direction, so the focal length is positive. A wrong answer indicates the student has memorised "convex = negative" from a different sign convention (like the old real-is-positive convention) without understanding the Cartesian rule.

questions.q: The radius of curvature of a convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror in a car is 2.0 m. Calculate its focal length. Give the answer with proper sign and unit.
questions.a: Given: R = +2.0 m (centre of curvature behind mirror → positive in Cartesian convention). Formula: f = R/2. Substitution: f = (+2.0 m)/2 = +1.0 m. The focal length is +1.0 m. A wrong answer with a negative sign shows sign convention error; missing unit or using cm without conversion shows unit negligence.

questions.q: Two convex mirrors A and B have radii of curvature 30 cm and 50 cm respectively. Which mirror has a longer focal length? How does the focal length affect the field of view?
questions.a: Mirror B (R = 50 cm) has focal length f = 25 cm; Mirror A has f = 15 cm. Mirror B has longer focal length. A longer focal length (less curved mirror) gives a narrower field of view but larger image size; a shorter focal length (more curved) gives a wider field of view but smaller images. A wrong choice reveals inability to connect focal length with curvature and practical consequence.

questions.q: A diagram shows a convex mirror with pole P, centre of curvature C, and a point F marked on the principal axis in front of the mirror (between P and C). A student labels F as the principal focus. Evaluate this diagram and correct the error.
questions.a: The diagram is incorrect. For a convex mirror, the principal focus must be behind the mirror (on the opposite side of the reflecting surface), not in front. The point F should be located behind the mirror such that PF = PC/2. The student has confused convex with concave mirror focus position. This error shows lack of visualisation of virtual focus.

questions.q: Design a simple activity using a convex mirror (e.g., a shiny metal bowl), a laser pointer, and a screen to demonstrate that the principal focus of a convex mirror is virtual. Describe the steps and what you would observe.
questions.a: Steps: (1) Fix the convex mirror on a stand. (2) Direct a laser beam parallel to the principal axis onto the mirror. (3) Observe the reflected beam diverges. (4) Place a screen in front of the mirror — no sharp spot forms. (5) Extend the reflected ray backward using a ruler or string behind the mirror; the extensions meet at a point F behind the mirror. Observation: The focus cannot be captured on a screen in front; it is virtual. A poor answer that tries to catch the focus on a screen in front shows misunderstanding of virtual vs real focus.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The principal focus of a convex mirror is the point on the principal axis where incident rays parallel to the principal axis appear to diverge from after ______.
Fill in the blank: Observe the outer curved surface of a stainless steel spoon or a car's side-view mirror — you see a ______, upright image of the surroundings.

Fill in the blank: The focal length (f) is the distance between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F); for a convex mirror, the focus lies behind the mirror, so the focal length is taken as positive in the Cartesian sign convention and is equal to half the radius of curvature (f = R/______).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can draw a ray diagram showing parallel rays reflecting off a convex mirror and correctly locate the virtual principal focus behind the mirror, and can calculate the focal length given the radius of curvature (or vice versa) using f = R/2 with correct sign and units.
